ch04.d.launch: Throw from the ground at an angle, or horizontally from a height $h$
ch04.d.theta: Angle between the initial velocity and the horizontal
ch04.d.v0: Speed at the moment of release
ch04.d.vectors: Velocity $v$ on the ball and its components $v_x$, $v_y$ on the shadows
ch04.launch.ground: From the ground at an angle
ch04.goal.split: Projectile motion = uniform motion in $x$ + uniformly accelerated motion in $y$ (acceleration $-g$)
ch04.goal.indep: The two motions are independent; they share only the time $t$
ch04.obs.x: Shadow on the $x$ axis: equal distances in equal times (evenly spaced strobe marks), constant $v_x$
ch04.obs.y: Shadow on the $y$ axis: moves like a ball thrown straight up; $v_y = 0$ at the top
ch04.obs.cliff: Horizontal throw from $h$: the $y$ shadow is a ball dropped from the same height, so both land together, whatever the launch speed
ch04.obs.range: From the ground: the range is largest at 45°, and 30° and 60° give the same range
ch04.obs.g: Moon and Mars: same launch speed, smaller $g$, so longer flights and longer ranges
